chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, Al Sakuni, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) narrated, saying:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The pillars of disbelief are four: desire (al-raghbah), awe/fear (al-rahibah), resentment (al-sakhat), and anger (al-ghadab).'
ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars of disbelief according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) attributes to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) the identification of four psychological states as the cornerstones of disbelief. While 'raghba' (desire/attraction) and 'rahba' (awe/fear) are often viewed positively in general Islamic discourse, here they signify excessive attachment to worldly life and fear of it that distracts from divine reality. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on internal spiritual states (ahwal) as the root of external theological rejection, linking emotional balance directly to faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The corner-stones of the disbelief are four – the desire, and the awe, and the resentment, and the anger’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Holy Prophet has said, ‘The pillars of disbelief are four: Greed, Fear, Resentment and Anger.’”
